passages.text: So then, men ought to regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians.
Paul and his companions serve Christ.
People should see Paul and his companions as servants of Christ.
Paul and his companions manage the mysteries of God.
People should see Paul and his companions as stewards of God's mysteries.
passages.original: Οὕτως ἡμᾶς λογιζέσθω ἄνθρωπος ὡς ὑπηρέτας Χριστοῦ καὶ οἰκονόμους μυστηρίων Θεοῦ

passages.text: Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.
passages.sermon: A steward manages what belongs to someone else.\r\nGod requires stewards to be faithful.\r\nGod looks for faithfulness in every steward.
passages.original: ὧδε λοιπὸν ζητεῖται ἐν τοῖς οἰκονόμοις ἵνα πιστός τις εὑρεθῇ

passages.text: I care very little, however, if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I do not even judge myself.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a servant of Christ and a steward of the mysteries of God.
Paul does not care if you judge him.
Paul does not care if any human court judges him.
Paul does not judge himself.
passages.original: Ἐμοὶ δὲ εἰς ἐλάχιστόν ἐστιν ἵνα ὑφ’ ὑμῶν ἀνακριθῶ ἢ ὑπὸ ἀνθρωπίνης ἡμέρας ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἀνακρίνω

passages.text: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul says his conscience is clear.
A clear conscience does not make Paul innocent.
The Lord judges Paul.
passages.original: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐμαυτῷ σύνοιδα ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐν τούτῳ δεδικαίωμαι ὁ δὲ ἀνακρίνων με Κύριός ἐστιν

passages.text: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.
passages.sermon:
Do not judge anything before the right time.
Wait until the Lord comes.
The Lord will bring to light what is hidden in darkness.
The Lord will show the motives of people’s hearts.
Then each person will receive praise from God.
passages.original: Ὥστε μὴ πρὸ καιροῦ τι κρίνετε ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ ὁ Κύριος ὃς καὶ φωτίσει τὰ κρυπτὰ τοῦ σκότους καὶ φανερώσει τὰς βουλὰς τῶν καρδιῶν καὶ τότε ὁ ἔπαινος γενήσεται ἑκάστῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us not to go beyond what is written. Then you will not take pride in one man over another.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, I speak to you now.
I have used myself and Apollos as examples.
I did this for your benefit.
I want you to learn from us.
Do not go beyond what is written in Scripture.
If you follow this, you will not take pride in one person over another.
passages.original: Ταῦτα δέ ἀδελφοί μετεσχημάτισα εἰς ἐμαυτὸν καὶ Ἀπολλῶν δι’ ὑμᾶς ἵνα ἐν ἡμῖν μάθητε τό Μὴ ὑπὲρ ἃ γέγραπται ἵνα μὴ εἷς ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἑνὸς φυσιοῦσθε κατὰ τοῦ ἑτέρου

passages.text: For who makes you so superior? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?
passages.sermon:
God gives every good thing you have.
You did not earn these things by yourself.
No one is truly superior to another.
God is the one who gives gifts to each person.
You have nothing that you did not receive from God.
If you received it from God, you should not boast.
Do not act as if you gained it on your own.
passages.original: τίς γάρ σε διακρίνει τί δὲ ἔχεις ὃ οὐκ ἔλαβες εἰ δὲ καὶ ἔλαβες τί καυχᾶσαι ὡς μὴ λαβών

passages.text: Already you have all you want. Already you have become rich. Without us, you have become kings. How I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you!
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthian Christians.
Paul says you already have everything you want.
You already have become rich.
You have become kings without us.
I wish you truly were kings.
Then we could also be kings with you.
passages.original: ἤδη κεκορεσμένοι ἐστέ ἤδη ἐπλουτήσατε χωρὶς ἡμῶν ἐβασιλεύσατε καὶ ὄφελόν γε ἐβασιλεύσατε ἵνα καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμῖν συμβασιλεύσωμεν

passages.text: For it seems to me that God has displayed us apostles at the end of the procession, like prisoners appointed for death. We have become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels as well as to men.
passages.sermon:
God chose us apostles.
God put us last in line.
God made us like prisoners who face death.
We have become a spectacle.
The whole world watches us.
Angels watch us.
People watch us.
passages.original: δοκῶ γάρ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἐσχάτους ἀπέδειξεν ὡς ἐπιθανατίους ὅτι θέατρον ἐγενήθημεν τῷ κόσμῳ καὶ ἀγγέλοις καὶ ἀνθρώποις

passages.text: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are dishonored.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul and the other apostles serve Christ.
We are fools for Christ.
You are wise in Christ.
We are weak.
You are strong.
You are honored.
We are dishonored.
passages.original: Ἡμεῖς μωροὶ διὰ Χριστόν ὑμεῖς δὲ φρόνιμοι ἐν Χριστῷ ἡμεῖς ἀσθενεῖς ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰσχυροί ὑμεῖς ἔνδοξοι ἡμεῖς δὲ ἄτιμοι

passages.text: To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed, we are brutally treated, we are homeless.
passages.sermon:
We are apostles of Jesus Christ.
God has appointed us to suffer for Him.
To this very hour, we are hungry.
We are thirsty.
We do not have enough clothing.
People treat us harshly.
We do not have a home.
passages.original: ἄχρι τῆς ἄρτι ὥρας καὶ πεινῶμεν καὶ διψῶμεν καὶ γυμνιτεύομεν καὶ κολαφιζόμεθα καὶ ἀστατοῦμεν

passages.text: We work hard with our own hands. When we are vilified, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it; when we are slandered, we answer gently. Up to this moment we have become the scum of the earth, the refuse of the world.
passages.sermon:
We are apostles of Christ.
We work hard.
We use our own hands to labor.
People insult us.
We bless those who insult us.
People persecute us.
We endure persecution.
People slander us.
We answer gently when people slander us.
Up to this moment, people treat us as the scum of the earth.
We have become like the refuse of the world.
passages.original: καὶ κοπιῶμεν ἐργαζόμενοι ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσίν λοιδορούμενοι εὐλογοῦμεν διωκόμενοι ἀνεχόμεθα δυσφημούμενοι παρακαλοῦμεν ὡς περικαθάρματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐγενήθημεν πάντων περίψημα ἕως ἄρτι

passages.text: I am not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthians.
Paul loves them as his own children.
Paul does not want to shame them.
Paul writes these things to warn them.
Paul warns them because he loves them.
passages.original: Οὐκ ἐντρέπων ὑμᾶς γράφω ταῦτα ἀλλ’ ὡς τέκνα μου ἀγαπητὰ νουθετῶν

passages.text: Even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the believers in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul cares for the believers as a father cares for his children.
You may have many guardians in Christ.
You do not have many fathers.
In Christ Jesus, I became your father through the gospel.
passages.original: ἐὰν γὰρ μυρίους παιδαγωγοὺς ἔχητε ἐν Χριστῷ ἀλλ’ οὐ πολλοὺς πατέρας ἐν γὰρ Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς ἐγέννησα

passages.text: Therefore I urge you to imitate me.
passages.sermon:
I am Paul.
\r\nI am your spiritual father in Christ Jesus.
\r\nI love you as my beloved children.
\r\nI urge you now.
\r\nImitate me.
passages.original: παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε

passages.text: That is why I have sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which is exactly what I teach everywhere in every church.
passages.sermon:
I have sent Timothy to you.
Timothy is my child.
I love Timothy.
Timothy is faithful in the Lord.
Timothy will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus.
I teach this way of life everywhere.
I teach it in every church.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἔπεμψα ὑμῖν Τιμόθεον ὅς ἐστίν μου τέκνον ἀγαπητὸν καὶ πιστὸν ἐν Κυρίῳ ὃς ὑμᾶς ἀναμνήσει τὰς ὁδούς μου τὰς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ καθὼς πανταχοῦ ἐν πάσῃ ἐκκλησίᾳ διδάσκω

passages.text: Some of you have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you.
passages.sermon: Some of you have become arrogant.\r\nYou act as if I am not coming to you.
passages.original: Ὡς μὴ ἐρχομένου δέ μου πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐφυσιώθησάν τινες

passages.text: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only what these arrogant people are saying, but what power they have.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul plans to visit the church soon.
Paul will come quickly, if the Lord allows it.
Some people in the church are arrogant.
Paul will find out what these arrogant people are saying.
Paul will also find out what power these people have.
passages.original: ἐλεύσομαι δὲ ταχέως πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος θελήσῃ καὶ γνώσομαι οὐ τὸν λόγον τῶν πεφυσιωμένων ἀλλὰ τὴν δύναμιν

passages.text: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.
passages.sermon: The kingdom of God is not about words.\r\nThe kingdom of God is about power.
passages.original: οὐ γὰρ ἐν λόγῳ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀλλ’ ἐν δυνάμει

passages.text: Which do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit?
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul asks the Corinthians a question.
He says, “What do you want?”
He asks, “Should I come to you with a rod?”
A rod means discipline and correction.
He also asks, “Or should I come in love?”
He adds, “Should I come with a gentle spirit?”
Paul offers them a choice between discipline and gentleness.
passages.original: τί θέλετε ἐν ῥάβδῳ ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἢ ἐν ἀγάπῃ πνεύματί τε πραΰτητος
